transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is my eating, doctor. I’ll start with something comforting, like food from the pot, and I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough now,” but then my hand just goes right back in like it doesn’t listen to me. It feels like I can’t make myself stop once I get going.

And you know, I never used to talk about things like this… people in my family, we just kept busy and didn’t make a fuss. But it’s been bothering me, that feeling of not being in charge of my own hand.
Do you often find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal or eating until you feel uncomfortably full, especially during these times when you feel like you can't stop eating?

Yes… yes, I do eat fast when it happens. Funny thing is, I’ve always been a slow eater—my sisters used to tease me because I’d still be working on my plate when everyone else was clearing the table. But lately, when I get like that, I’m just standing there by the counter, taking bite after bite, barely even tasting it before the next one is already in my mouth. It makes me feel embarrassed, honestly.
Do you have episodes where you feel you’re eating a very large amount of food in a short period of time, even if you aren’t hungry, and feel unable to control your eating during those times?

Yes… yes, that does happen. Like some afternoons, after choir practice—or if I’ve been out in the garden pulling weeds, you know, the tomatoes need so much fussing—I’ll come in and fix myself a plate of rice and beans, or maybe chicken stew if I made some.

And I tell myself it’s just a regular plate, but then I go back. Then again. Before I really stop and think, it’s like I’ve eaten enough for two or three meals. It makes me feel ashamed, because I’m not always even hungry like that… I just keep going.
Do these episodes where you feel unable to control your eating cause you significant distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

It does upset me, yes. I mean, I still do my things — I go to Mass, I sing with the choir, I keep the house picked up. I’m not just… you know, lying around doing nothing.

But after one of those afternoons, I get so embarrassed. I’ll think about calling my cousin or answering the phone, and then I just don’t. I stay in, keep to myself. It’s silly maybe, because nobody even saw me, but I feel like they can tell somehow.
After these times when you feel like you’ve eaten too much, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… I’m not sure I do anything like that. I don’t really know what you’d count, exactly. I mean, I might tell myself I’ll be “better tomorrow,” you know, have soup or keep busy with the laundry, but making myself sick or taking something… no, I don’t think that’s something I do.

Exercise, well, at my age, “a lot more” would be a big word. I walk around the yard some, and if the weeds are bad I’ll be out there longer than I meant to be, but that’s more because the garden gets away from me, not because I’m trying to undo eating.
How often do these times when you feel like you can't control your eating happen? Do they happen at least once a week, or more often?

Yes… I’d say most weeks now. Since my friend passed, the afternoons got so quiet, you know? We used to talk after choir sometimes, or I’d tell her about the garden—my beans did terrible one year, just terrible.

But, yes, to answer you… it’s usually once or twice a week, mostly those quiet afternoons after choir or when I’ve been out gardening.
